ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the AC power supply u, with the upper end connected to the upper wire node and the lower end connected to the bottom-left wire. HL1 is located in the upper branch at the upper right, and HL2 is located in the lower branch at the lower left. The middle vertical branch has a diode connected between the upper and lower black nodes; the right vertical branch also has a diode connected, and together with the upper branch where HL1 is located and the bottom node forms the right-side loop. Reasoning: Analyze according to the two AC half-cycles. When the upper power-supply terminal is positive, the middle diode is forward-conducting, and the current goes from the upper end through the middle diode to the lower node, then passes through HL2 back to the lower end of the power supply; at this time, the diode in the right-side branch is reverse-cutoff, so HL1 has no current, and HL1 does not light. When the lower power-supply terminal is positive, the middle diode is reverse-cutoff, the right-side diode is forward-conducting, and the current passes through HL2, the right-side diode, and HL1 in series to form a loop, so HL1 and HL2 both have current in this half-cycle. Thus it can be seen that HL2 has current passing through it in both half-cycles, while HL1 has current passing through it in only one half-cycle. The two lamps are the same; the greater the average power, the brighter it is, so HL2's average power is greater.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, which lamp is brighter, HL1 or HL2?

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure, then analyze the two AC half-cycles. When the upper source terminal is positive, the central diode is forward biased, so current goes through the central diode and then through HL2 back to the source; the right branch diode blocks, so HL1 is off. When the lower source terminal is positive, the central diode blocks and the right-side diode conducts, so current goes through HL2, the right-side diode, and HL1 in series. Thus HL2 carries current in both half-cycles, while HL1 carries current only in one half-cycle. Therefore HL2 has the larger average power and is brighter.

推理：按两个交流半周分析。上端电源端为正时，中间二极管正向导通，电流从上端经中间二极管到下方节点，再经过 HL2 回到电源下端；此时右侧支路的二极管反向截止，所以 HL1 没有电流，HL1 不亮。下端电源端为正时，中间二极管反向截止，右侧二极管正向导通，电流经过 HL2、右侧二极管和 HL1 串联形成回路，因此 HL1 和 HL2 在这一半周都有电流。由此可见，HL2 在两个半周都有电流通过，而 HL1 只在一个半周有电流通过。两个灯相同，平均功率越大越亮，所以 HL2 的平均功率更大。

method.method_draft: Convert the circuit into two equivalent circuits, one for each polarity of the AC source. For the polarity that forward-biases the middle diode, the equivalent circuit contains HL2 as the load and excludes HL1 because the right diode is open. For the opposite polarity, the middle diode is open and the right diode is a short, giving a series path containing both HL2 and HL1. Compute/compare qualitatively the average power: HL2 dissipates power during the middle-diode half-cycle and also during the right-diode half-cycle, while HL1 dissipates power only during the right-diode half-cycle. Hence the time-averaged power of HL2 is greater, so HL2 is brighter.
